issues.legal_issue: A fatal assault committed without premeditation during a sudden fight, without cruel or unusual conduct, falls within the exception for culpable homicide that is not murder.
material_facts: The appellant arrived with cattle at a field where the deceased and other labourers were working, and an altercation followed an objection to the cattle grazing there.
There was no premeditation for the assault; during the sudden fight, the appellant delivered one blow with a pharsa to the deceased’s head.
The deceased died from the injury, but the appellant inflicted no further injuries, left after the blow, and did not assault the other people present.
issues.conclusion: The exception to murder applied, and the appellant was guilty of culpable homicide punishable under Section 304 Part I IPC, rather than murder under Section 302 IPC.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC and Section 304 Part I IPC. It treated the absence of premeditation, the sudden fight, the single blow, and the absence of cruel or unusual conduct as establishing that the offence fell within Exception 4. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_after_conviction_was_upgraded and no_premeditation and sudden_fight and single_head_blow and no_cruel_or_unusual_conduct

predicates.criminal_appeal_after_conviction_was_upg: The case is a criminal appeal following a higher court’s upgrade of a conviction to a more serious offence.
predicates.no_premeditation: The assault was not planned before the parties encountered one another.
predicates.sudden_fight: The assault occurred during a fight that arose suddenly after an altercation.
predicates.single_head_blow: The assailant delivered one blow to the victim’s head and inflicted no further injury.
predicates.no_cruel_or_unusual_conduct: The assailant did not continue the attack or assault the other people present.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows an upgrade to a more serious conviction and the assault was unplanned, arose from a sudden fight, consisted of one head blow, and involved no cruel or unusual conduct, the offence is culpable homicide rather than murder.

issues.legal_issue: A higher court errs in reversing a trial court’s reasoned finding on the degree of an offence when it does not displace the reasons supporting that finding.
material_facts: The trial court found the evidence established the fatal assault but concluded that the circumstances brought the offence within the exception to murder, convicting the appellant of the lesser homicide offence.
The State appealed the acquittal on the murder charge, and the High Court upgraded the conviction to murder without dispelling the trial court’s reasons for its conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in setting aside the trial court’s conviction for the lesser homicide offence and upgrading the conviction to murder.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held, on these facts, that the High Court was wrong to interfere with the trial court’s reasoned conclusion when it had not dispelled the reasons supporting that conclusion. No provision or earlier case is cited for this point.

predicates.state_appeal_challenged_acquittal_on_gre: The prosecution appealed the trial court’s acquittal on a more serious charge after the trial court convicted the accused of a lesser offence.
predicates.trial_court_gave_reasons_for_lesser_offe: The trial court explained why the evidence and circumstances supported conviction for the lesser offence rather than the greater offence.
predicates.higher_court_reversed_without_dispelling: The higher court replaced the trial court’s conclusion without rebutting the reasons the trial court had given.

issues.definition: If the prosecution appeals an acquittal on a greater offence, the trial court has reasoned its finding of a lesser offence, and the higher court reverses without dispelling those reasons, the higher court’s reversal is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence for a fatal culpable-homicide offence must be increased when the original sentence is grossly inadequate and unreasonable in the circumstances.
material_facts: The trial court imposed two years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 500 for the culpable-homicide conviction.

The Supreme Court found that sentence grossly inadequate and unreasonable and, considering the circumstances, substituted six years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,000, with four months’ rigorous imprisonment in default of payment.
issues.conclusion: The sentence was increased to six years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,000, with four months’ rigorous imprisonment in default of payment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the punishment imposed was grossly inadequate and unreasonable in light of the circumstances, and substituted what it considered a proper sentence. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for the sentencing decision.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and fatal_culpable_homicide and original_sentence_was_brief and circumstances_make_sentence_grossly_inadequate

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The case is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction and its sentence.
predicates.fatal_culpable_homicide: The accused was convicted of a culpable-homicide offence that resulted in the victim’s death.
predicates.original_sentence_was_brief: The trial court imposed a comparatively short custodial sentence and a fine.
predicates.circumstances_make_sentence_grossly_inad: The circumstances of the offence make the punishment originally imposed grossly inadequate and unreasonable.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a fatal culpable-homicide conviction, the original sentence is brief, and the circumstances make it grossly inadequate, the sentence is increased to an adequate level.
